text.text: Vibeprint: how does an iPad sketch survive a page reload?

New engineers · Direct LAN only: iPad browser edits, local daemon memory, debounced canvas.json save, reload snapshot and startup
read.

Draws ink, queues
unacked ops,
reconnects

Saved shapes; read
only at daemon
start

Key: frames = trust/deployment zones; box = runtime actor/process; cylinder = stored state. Arrows: caller → recipient, response
included; dotted = local command/I/O; dashed = async; solid = sync. Flow type is also written on each arrow.

The daemon acks an op once it is in
memory and saves canvas.json 800ms
after the last edit (flushes on
shutdown). A daemon crash inside that
window loses those edits.

Socket drops retry with 500ms→10s
backoff; unacked ops are replayed on
the next snapshot. Pending ops live
only in page memory, so a full reload
before ack loses them.

LAN HTTP/WS needs the ?t= token
(then an HttpOnly cookie) or gets 401.
Unparseable canvas.json stops daemon
start (restore from git); bad shapes are
skipped and logged.
Outside this view: Relay, MCP server, AI map generation and git checkpoints; Marks/chat persistence and the legacy tldraw import.
